stories.title: This design software reimagines everyday objects as self-aware devices
stories.summary: MIT researchers developed X-Hinges, software that helps design 3D-printed objects with built-in sensors. The tricky part is separating the sensors’ signals from interference caused by the wire-like connections around them. The tool places two different materials in the design to reduce that interference. The researchers describe objects such as lamps and gloves that respond to touch, as well as small robots and toys. It is an understandable electronics problem: make an object sense what someone is doing, then get a clear signal out of it.

"This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration," Obama told crowds in Ohio on Saturday. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump sought to energise voters at a rally in Georgia, after he cast an early ballot alongside First Lady Melania Trump in Florida. Early voting has already begun ahead of the 3 November elections, which will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's presidency.
